analysis.title: Flutter Entertainment (FLUT) 3Q26 Review: Resetting mid-term US profitability expectations
key_insights: GS lowers estimates after 3Q26 results on a significantly weaker US profitability outlook. Buy rating retained, 12m price target cut to $120 from $162 (about 45% upside vs $81.79 price).
3Q26 was broadly in line excluding unfavourable sports results, but FY26 guidance was cut again including those adverse sports results.
US trends were mixed: better underlying sportsbook volume trends and softer iGaming trends.
Management now expects promotional investment to stay higher into 2027 and marketing intensity to be significantly higher than previously expected, which resets FY27 US expectations.
Flutter suspended its buyback programme to prioritise organic investment and deleveraging.
GS cuts mid-term Group EBITDA forecasts by mid-teens percentages, driven by the US business. Mid-term EPS estimates fall 26% on average.
GS lowers its US iGaming growth outlook because its data trackers show a recent industry growth deceleration and a slight softening of Flutter's market share.
GS FY27 US revenue/EBITDA forecasts are $7,945mn/$846mn, both slightly below Visible Alpha consensus, which has been revised down about 20% since the 3Q print.

For International, GS assumes an indefinite closure of operations in Brazil and reflects unfavourable sports results in 2H26. Mid-term International EBITDA forecasts are broadly unchanged, with +3% upside to consensus International EBITDA in FY27E.
GS base case is for buybacks to resume during 2028 and grow from 2029, as Flutter delevers to the upper end of its 2-2.5x target range by FY28 year-end.

Re-rating over 12 months depends on (1) the US product roadmap and investment plans improving performance, particularly in online sportsbook (OSB), and (2) evidence of returns from FanDuel Predicts and the earnings potential from market making.
Prediction market progress (excluding market making) has been weaker than expected.
At 7x EV/EBITDA and a 10% FCF yield on GS 2028 forecasts, GS sees asymmetric risk/reward.
GS 2027 EBITDA is meaningfully below the CMD guidance and prior GS expectations, but GS believes Group EBITDA can grow at a mid-teens rate longer term with US EBITDA doubling over 2027-30E.
Price target uses a SOTP: US at 10x EV/EBITDA on NTM+4 estimates (from 11.75x), discounted at a 12.6% WACC (from 11.9%). International and central costs use 9x EV/EBITDA on NTM+1.
FLUT shares are down 63.2% over 12 months and 22.1% over 3 months.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $120 from $162 on lower US profitability estimates, a lower US valuation multiple and a higher WACC. Buy retained on asymmetric risk/reward at 7x 2028 EV/EBITDA.

sector_views.rationale: US promotional intensity and marketing costs stay higher for longer, and US iGaming industry growth has decelerated. GS still sees US EBITDA doubling over 2027-30E.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (reported 11/4 or 11/5, 2026) was broadly in line excluding unfavourable sports results. FY26 guidance was cut again including adverse sports results.
GS FY26E adjusted EPS $3.81 new vs $4.72 old. FY27E $5.75 vs $7.61. FY28E $7.77 vs $10.73 (GS estimates, not reported).
GS FY26E adjusted EBITDA $2,467mn vs $2,648mn old (-7%). FY27E $2,932mn vs $3,382mn (-13%). FY28E $3,435mn vs $4,083mn (-16%).
GS FY27E US revenue $7,945mn and US EBITDA $846mn vs Visible Alpha consensus $8,008mn and $868mn (consensus median, revised down about 20% post print).
GS FY27E adjusted EPS $5.75 vs VA consensus $5.20 (+11%). FY27E adjusted EBITDA $2,932mn vs consensus $2,896mn (+1%).
GS FY26E US EBITDA $703mn is largely consistent with the mid-point of company guidance.

trade_ideas.description: Long FLUT, Buy rating with $120 12-month price target
trade_ideas.rationale: Mid-term expectations have been significantly reset and the stock trades at 7x EV/EBITDA and a 10% FCF yield on GS lowered 2028 forecasts.
trade_ideas.risk: Regulation, US execution including prediction markets, intensified competition, changes in consumer preferences, a less favourable macro environment, M&A integration/execution, and failure of IT systems/loss of customer data.

risk_factors: Failure of IT systems/loss of customer data
Higher-for-longer US promotional and marketing intensity
Continued US market share losses for FanDuel
vol_and_positioning: FLUT trades at 7x EV/EBITDA and a 10% FCF yield on GS lowered 2028 forecasts.
Shares are down 63.2% absolute and 67.6% relative to the S&P 500 over 12 months.
geopolitical: Flutter assumed to have an indefinite closure of operations in Brazil.
Regulatory and tax developments in the UK, India and Brazil are cited as pressures on International.

tension_points.bull_case: Expectations are reset, the stock trades at 7x 2028 EV/EBITDA with a 10% FCF yield, and GS sees US EBITDA doubling over 2027-30E with Group EBITDA growing at a mid-teens rate.
tension_points.bear_case: Promotional intensity and marketing costs stay higher for longer, US iGaming growth is decelerating with slight share loss, and prediction market returns are unproven.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure of the US product roadmap to improve online sportsbook performance and lack of evidence of returns from FanDuel Predicts and market making would undermine a 12-month re-rating.
